title.rendered: When Are The IB Exams? A Complete 2025 Schedule

content.rendered:
For students enrolled in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (IBDP), knowing when exams take place is essential for effective planning and preparation. IB exams are typically held during the May session, with a secondary session in November for select students or resits. 

Each subject has a specific schedule and duration, and understanding the exact dates helps students allocate sufficient study time, manage their workload, and reduce stress during the exam period.

At Ignite Training Institute in Dubai, UAE, students receive expert guidance to navigate the IB curriculum with confidence. With experienced IB tutors specializing in IBDP and MYP subjects, Ignite provides tailored coaching, exam strategies, and structured study plans to help students prepare effectively for their exams.

When Are The IB Exams Held Each Year?

The International Baccalaureate (IB) exams are a crucial part of the IB Diploma Programme (DP), and knowing their schedule is essential for effective preparation. IB exams are held twice a year, in May and November, depending on the school’s schedule and regional requirements.

1. May Session

The May session is the main exam period and is the most common for students worldwide. Exams typically begin in the first two weeks of May and can run for about two to three weeks, depending on the number of subjects a student is taking. This session is primarily for students in the Northern Hemisphere, including most IB schools in Europe, Asia, and North America.

2. November Session

The November session is smaller and usually caters to students in the Southern Hemisphere or schools following a different academic calendar. These exams generally take place in the first two weeks of November. While fewer students sit for the November session, the structure and rigor of the exams remain the same as in May.

When Are The IB Exams In 2026?

The May 2026 IB exam session is set to run from Friday, 24 April 2026, to Wednesday, 20 May 2026. 

The November 2026 IB exam session is scheduled to begin around Friday, 26 October 2026 (or thereabouts, depending on region) and run into November. 

Students will be assigned to one of several exam “zones” (based on time zones/regions) with morning and afternoon sessions differing slightly by region.

Related: IB Subject Choices: A 2026 Guide For Subject Combinations

How Students Can Effectively Manage Their IB Exam Schedule?

Managing your IB exam schedule effectively is crucial for maximizing performance and reducing stress. The IB Diploma Programme covers multiple subjects, often with exams spanning several weeks, making organization and planning essential. Here are strategies to help students handle their IB exam timetable efficiently:

1. Know Your Exam Dates Early

As soon as the official IB exam schedule is released by your school, mark all exam dates on a calendar. Highlight higher-weighted or more challenging subjects to allocate extra preparation time. Knowing your schedule in advance allows you to plan study blocks, revision sessions, and breaks strategically.

2. Create A Study Plan

Break down your preparation into daily and weekly study goals. Allocate more time to subjects that are difficult or have exams scheduled earlier in the session. Use techniques like active recall, spaced repetition, and timed practice tests to reinforce knowledge and improve retention.

3. Prioritize Rest & Self-Care

While studying is important, it’s equally crucial to maintain sleep, nutrition, and exercise routines. Cramming all night can lead to burnout and reduce performance. Short breaks during study sessions help improve focus and consolidate memory.

4. Simulate Exam Conditions

Practice past papers under timed conditions similar to the actual IB exams. This builds familiarity with the exam format and improves time management during real tests. For subjects with multiple papers, simulate the sequence of exams to get comfortable with transitioning between sections.

5. Use A Subject Rotation Strategy

Instead of studying one subject intensively for long periods, rotate between subjects in a single day. This keeps your mind fresh, reinforces learning across topics, and prevents fatigue. Pair harder subjects with easier ones to balance cognitive load.

6. Stay Organized During The Exam Session

Keep all exam materials, stationery, calculators, and identification ready in advance. Arrive at the exam center early to reduce anxiety and allow time to settle in. During the session, keep track of the time per section to ensure you can complete all questions.

FAQs

1. How long do IB exams last?

The duration of IB exams depends on the subject and level. Most exams last 1.5 to 2.5 hours, with Higher Level (HL) exams typically longer than Standard Level (SL) exams. Certain subjects, like Language and Literature or sciences, may include multiple papers or components, extending the total exam time.

2. When do students receive their IB exam schedule?

Schools provide students with the official IB exam timetable several months before the session, usually by February for the May session and by September for the November session. This schedule includes dates, times, and exam room assignments for each subject.

3. Can IB exam dates vary by school or region?

While the IB sets the official exam session, exact exam times and schedules may vary slightly depending on the school or time zone. Students should always confirm with their school’s IB coordinator for the most accurate schedule.

4. How can students prepare for the IB exam schedule?

Students should plan their revision around the official exam dates, prioritize subjects with earlier exams, and practice timed past papers. Creating a study timetable that aligns with the IB schedule ensures effective preparation without last-minute stress.

Conclusion

Understanding when the IB exams take place is a key part of planning your academic success. With exams typically scheduled in May and November, early preparation and smart time management can make all the difference in achieving top scores. By keeping track of important dates, organizing the study schedule, and practicing consistently, students can approach their IB exams with confidence and clarity.
